- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags behind true price movements; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the first 5–7 days of the horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for the following 3–7 days.
- Mean reversion is evident when model holds high prices for 5+ days without correction; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment shifts.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum (last 7–10 days); if sentiment turns positive late in the history, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the final 7 days of the horizon.
